text:
Predicates:
Yelp(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp’s recommendations.
NegativeReviews(x) ::: x receives many negative reviews.
Rating(x, y) ::: x has a rating of y.
TakeOut(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
Popular(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
Subway ::: Subway restaurant.
Premises:
Yelp(x) → ¬NegativeReviews(x) ::: If the restaurant is listed in Yelp’s recommendations, then the restaurant does not receive many negative reviews.
Rating(x, y) ∧ y > 9 → Yelp(x) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than 9 are listed in Yelp’s recommendations.
¬TakeOut(x) ∧ NegativeReviews(x) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
Popular(x) → Rating(x, y) ∧ y > 9 ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than 9.
Rating(subway, y) ∧ y > 9 ∨ Popular(subway) ::: Subway has a rating greater than 9 or is popular among local residents.
Conclusion:
TakeOut(subway) ∧ NegativeReviews(subway) → Rating(subway, y) ∧ y > 9 ∧ ¬TakeOut(subway) ::: If Subway provides take-out service and receives many negative reviews, then its rating is greater than 9 and it does not provide take-out service.
